name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 1: Fullness at the two points where the breath arises
method_summary: The supreme [Goddess], whose nature is emission (visarga), sounds forth as prāṇa above and as jīva (the in-breath) below; by dwelling on and filling the two places where they arise, the state of fullness (bharitā sthiti) comes about.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 24 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Commentators identify the two places as the heart and the dvādaśānta (Kaumudī: 'utpattau dvādaśānte dvitīye hṛdi'). First dhāraṇā in Ānandabhaṭṭa's count as well.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 10: The same method on a void, a wall or a worthy vessel
method_summary: By this very method, contemplation on anything whatever - on a void, on a wall, on an excellent person (pātra) - dissolves of itself and grants the boon.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 100: Neither attachment nor aversion
method_summary: One should not cultivate aversion anywhere, nor attachment anywhere; in the middle, free of attachment and aversion, Brahman spreads.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 101: The unknowable and the void as Bhairava
method_summary: What is unknowable, ungraspable, void, what lies in non-being - all that is to be contemplated as Bhairava; at its end, awakening arises.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 102: The mind in outer space
method_summary: Placing the mind in outer space - eternal, supportless, void, pervasive, free of limitation - one enters the spaceless.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 103: Letting go of each object the moment the mind goes to it
method_summary: Wherever the mind goes, abandoning that very thing at that very moment, by not letting it settle, one becomes waveless.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 104: Continuous utterance of the word 'Bhairava'
method_summary: 'He makes all resound through fear (bhayā ... ravayati), he gives all, he pervades the whole' - by continuously uttering the word 'Bhairava' [with this sense], one becomes Śiva.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 105: At the thought 'I' and 'mine'
method_summary: When notions such as 'I', 'this is mine' arise, the mind goes to the supportless; impelled by meditation on that, one becomes calm.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 106: Contemplating the words 'eternal', 'all-pervading', 'supportless'
method_summary: Meditating at every moment on the words 'eternal', 'all-pervading', 'supportless', 'pervasive', 'lord of all', according to their meaning, one attains one's aim.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 107: 'What reality has a magic show?'
method_summary: 'All this, without reality, stands like a magic show; what reality has a magic show?' - by firmness in this, one goes to peace.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 133 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Illusion imagery used as a contemplation; relevant to the Advaita/Śaiva dispute on the world.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 108: The unchanging self: the world as void
method_summary: For the unchanging self, where is knowledge, where is action? External things depend on knowledge; therefore this world is void.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 109: 'No bondage, no liberation for me'
method_summary: 'For me there is no bondage, no liberation; these are bugbears for the frightened; this [world] is a reflection in the intellect, like the sun in waters.'
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 135 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). The Kaumudī reads 'bālasyaitā vibhīṣikāḥ' (bugbears for a child).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 11: The mind within the skull, eyes closed
method_summary: Placing the mind within the skull and remaining with eyes closed, gradually, through the mind's steadiness, one discerns the highest object.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 110: Withdrawing from the senses into the self
method_summary: All contact with pleasure, pain and the like comes through the doors of the senses; so, abandoning the senses, one abides in oneself, established in one's own self.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 111: Knowledge and the known as one
method_summary: Knowledge reveals everything, and the self is the revealer through everything; because they have a single nature, knowledge and the known are to be contemplated as one.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 112: Dissolution of mind, awareness, power and self
method_summary: When the four - mind, awareness (cetanā), power (śakti) and self (ātman) - have dissolved, beloved, then there is Bhairava's form.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 138 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Kaumudī glosses: mind = manas, cetanā = intellect (buddhi), śakti = the breath-power, ātman = the limited individual.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 12: The central channel like a lotus fibre
method_summary: The central channel (madhyanāḍī), situated in the middle, [is to be meditated on] in the form of a lotus fibre; by that goddess, meditated as inner space, the God shines forth.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 13: Closing the sense-doors: the bindu between the brows
method_summary: Blocking the eyes with the 'weapon' of the hands, piercing at the brows and closing the doors [of the senses]: when the point (bindu) is seen and gradually dissolves, in its midst is the supreme state.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 36 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Resembles the haṭha ṣaṇmukhī mudrā (see equivalents).

equivalents.note: Closing the sense-openings with the hands; the VBT adds the seen bindu

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 14: The bindu like a subtle spark, at the crest or in the heart
method_summary: For one who meditates on the point (bindu) - shaped like a subtle fiery mark arising from agitation within the light-abode (dhāma) - at the end of the crest (śikhānta) or in the heart, at the end of dissolution there is absorption.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 15: The unstruck sound (anāhata)
method_summary: One who is immersed in the Sound-Brahman - the unstruck (anāhata), unbroken sound, [heard] in the ear as a vessel, rushing like a river - attains the supreme Brahman.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 38 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). 'pātrakarṇe' is read differently in the recensions.

equivalents.note: Absorption in the inner unstruck sound

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 16: Uttering Oṃ and resting in the void at its end
method_summary: By uttering the praṇava (Oṃ) and the like, and contemplating the void at the end of its prolonged (pluta) sound, one goes to voidness by the supreme void power, O Bhairavī.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 39 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Kaumudī: the sixteenth (ṣoḍaśī) dhāraṇā - agrees with this count.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 17: The void before and after any sound
method_summary: One should contemplate the beginning and the end of any sound (varṇa) whatever; by the void [power] such a person becomes void, of the form of the void.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 18: The fading sounds of stringed instruments
method_summary: In the long, successive sounds of stringed and other instruments, one whose mind is on nothing else becomes, at the end of each, of the form of the supreme space.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 19: A seed-mantra dissolved into its subtle phases and the void
method_summary: Of any compound seed-mantra (piṇḍamantra), by [uttering] its gross letters in order and then, through the half-moon (ardhendu), the point (bindu), the resonance (nāda) and its end, by uttering the void, one becomes Śiva.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 2: The two voids at the turning points of the breath
method_summary: When the breath, moving inward or outward, does not turn back from the two spaces [at its ends], thus, O Bhairavī, the form of Bhairava is revealed through Bhairavī.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 25 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Kaumudī counts this 'the second' (dvitīyā).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 20: The body as space in all directions at once
method_summary: One should contemplate space in all directions simultaneously in one's own body; for one whose mind is free of thought-constructs, everything becomes space.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 43 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Kaumudī: 'now he states the twentieth (viṃśatitamī) dhāraṇā'.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 21: The voids above, at the root and in the heart
method_summary: Whoever contemplates simultaneously the void 'behind/above' (pṛṣṭha) and the void at the root becomes void-minded through the power independent of the body (44). One should contemplate steadily the void above, the void at the root and the void in the heart; from this simultaneous freedom from thought, the thought-free state arises (45).
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 44-45 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Grouped: the Kaumudī recension (KSTS 9) has one verse combining 44a and 45b.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 22: Voidness in a part of the body, for a moment
method_summary: One should contemplate voidness in [any] part of the body even for a moment; free of thought-constructs, one comes to share the nature of the thought-free.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 23: The body's substance pervaded by space
method_summary: O doe-eyed one, one should contemplate all the substance within the body as pervaded by space; then that contemplation of his becomes steady.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 24: The skin as a wall with nothing within
method_summary: One should contemplate the skin as a wall enclosing the body, with nothing inside it; meditating thus, one comes to partake of what cannot be meditated upon.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 25: The space of the heart-lotus
method_summary: One whose senses are dissolved in the space of the heart, dwelling in the middle of the closed lotus, with mind on nothing else, O fortunate one, attains the supreme fortune.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 26: Dissolving the mind in the dvādaśānta
method_summary: By dissolving the mind in the dvādaśānta of one's own body on all sides, for one of firm understanding the mark of reality becomes firm.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 27: Casting the mind into the dvādaśānta at any time
method_summary: However and wherever [one may be], one should cast the mind into the dvādaśānta; for one whose mental activity wanes moment by moment, an extraordinary state arises within days.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 28: One's own body burnt by the fire of time
method_summary: One should contemplate one's own 'city' (the body) as burnt by the fire of Kālāgni rising from the place of time (kālapada); at the end, the appearance of peace arises.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 52 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Commentators take 'the place of time' as the right big toe (interpretation).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 29: The whole world burnt
method_summary: In the same way, having meditated, by imagination, on the whole world as burnt, a person whose mind is on nothing else attains the supreme state of the person (pumbhāva).
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 3: Suspension of the breath-power in the centre
method_summary: When the power (śakti) in the form of breath neither goes out nor enters and [the centre] has expanded, through the absence of thought-constructs in the middle, by that [power] there is the state of Bhairava.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 30: Dissolving the tattvas into the subtler
method_summary: Having meditated on the tattvas of one's own body or of the world as dissolving into the subtle and the still subtler, at the end the Supreme (Parā) is revealed.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 31: The power, thick then thin, in the twelve and in the heart
method_summary: Having meditated on the power (śakti), [first] thick and [then] feeble, in the field of the twelve (dvādaśa), and entering and meditating in the heart, one is liberated and attains freedom (svātantrya).
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 32: The paths of the cosmos, gross to supreme
method_summary: One should contemplate the whole in the form of the path of worlds (bhuvanādhvan) and the other paths, step by step, in its gross, subtle and supreme condition, until at the end the mind dissolves.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 33: The Śiva-principle at the limits of the universe
method_summary: Having meditated, by the procedure of the paths, on the Śaiva principle at the limits of this entire universe on all sides, the great arising occurs.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 34: The universe as void
method_summary: O great Goddess, one should contemplate this universe as void; the mind dissolved there becomes fit for dissolution in That.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 35: Gazing into the space of a vessel
method_summary: One should cast one's gaze into a pot or other vessel, leaving aside its walls; entering its dissolution at once, by that dissolution one becomes one with it.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 36: Gazing at open, empty space
method_summary: One should cast the gaze on a place without trees, mountains, walls and the like; when the mental state dissolves, one whose activity has waned arises.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 37: The middle between two cognitions
method_summary: In the cognition of two things, having meditated, one should take refuge in the middle; abandoning both at once, reality shines in the middle.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 38: Between leaving one object and taking up another
method_summary: When one object has been abandoned, [if] consciousness, held back, does not go to another, then by being in the middle of them the contemplation blossoms greatly.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 39: Body and world as consciousness
method_summary: One should contemplate the whole body, or the world, as made of consciousness, all at once, with a thought-free mind: [then] the supreme arising.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 4: Peace at the end of retention, exhalation or inhalation
method_summary: Whenever [the breath-power] is held, expelled or drawn in, at the end of that the one called 'Peaceful' (Śānta) shines forth by means of the power.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 27 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Names retention (kumbhaka) without any duration or count; not an 'extreme retention' practice.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 40: The meeting of the two breaths
method_summary: Through the meeting of the two breaths, inside or outside, at the end the yogin becomes a vessel for the arising of the knowledge of sameness.

method_summary: Making the mind supportless, one should not entertain thought-constructs; then, when the self is the supreme self, [one is] Bhairava, O doe-eyed one.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 84: 'I am the omniscient, all-doing Lord'
method_summary: 'The supreme Lord is omniscient, all-doing and all-pervading; I am He, having the qualities of Śiva' - by firmness in this, one becomes Śiva.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 85: The universe as my waves
method_summary: As waves belong to water, flames to fire, rays to the sun, so these differentiated waves of the universe are mine, Bhairava's.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 86: Whirling until falling
method_summary: Whirling round and round with the body, by falling quickly to the ground, when the power of agitation ceases, the supreme state arises.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 87: When the mind's supports fail
method_summary: When, through incapacity or ignorance regarding the supports (objects), or through the dissolution of the mind, absorption into the power has arisen, at the end of its agitation [appears] the form of Bhairava.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 112 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Obscure; readings differ ('śaktyā ... dhyānāt' in the Kaumudī). Low confidence.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 88: The sampradāya: fixed eyes; closed ears and lower door
method_summary: Hear, O Goddess, this traditional teaching (sampradāya), which I declare fully: isolation (kaivalya) arises at once when the eyes are merely held still (113). Contracting the ears and likewise the lower door, meditating on the vowelless and consonantless, one enters the eternal Brahman (114).
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 113-114 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Grouped: v. 114 is absent from the Kaumudī recension's main text and is reported after the 'sampradāya' verse in one manuscript.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 89: Looking down into a well or deep pit
method_summary: Standing above a well or a great pit and gazing down, for one whose mind is free of thought-constructs, the mind dissolves at once, clearly.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 9: The five voids like the eyes of a peacock's feather
method_summary: For one who meditates on the five voids as [like] the variegated circles on a peacock's feathers, entry into the heart, the unsurpassed void, takes place.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 32 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). The 'five voids' are read by commentators as the five sense-faculties or five elements (interpretation).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 90: Wherever the mind goes, there is Śiva
method_summary: Wherever the mind goes, outside or within, there is the state of Śiva; since it is all-pervading, where could [the mind] go?
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 91: Consciousness shining through each sense
method_summary: Wherever, through the path of the senses, the consciousness of the all-pervading one is manifested, since it has the nature of that alone, by dissolution in consciousness there is fullness.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 92: Sneeze, fear, grief, flight, curiosity, hunger
method_summary: At the beginning and end of a sneeze, in fear, in grief, in a deep cave (or: in sobbing), when fleeing from battle, in curiosity, at the beginning and end of hunger, there is a state full of the being of Brahman.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 118 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). Compare Spandakārikā 1.22 (spanda found in intense states).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 93: Letting go of remembered objects and places
method_summary: When things are remembered, or a place is seen, one should let the mind go from it; making one's body supportless, the Lord spreads forth.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 94: Slowly withdrawing the gaze from an object
method_summary: Having placed the gaze on some object, one should slowly withdraw it; that knowledge, together with the mind, O Goddess, becomes an abode of the void.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 95: The understanding born of intense devotion
method_summary: The kind of understanding that arises in one who is dispassionate through the intensity of devotion - that is the eternal power of Śaṅkara; one should contemplate it; from that, [one is] Śiva.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 96: The voidness of all else when one object is known
method_summary: When one particular object is being known, there is voidness with regard to all other objects; meditating with the mind on that very [voidness], even while knowing, one becomes tranquil.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 97: Purity and impurity
method_summary: The purity prescribed by those of little knowledge is [regarded as] impurity in the vision of Śambhu; [in truth] nothing is pure or impure; therefore, free of thought-constructs, one becomes happy.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
notes: Verses 123 (KSTS 8 / GRETIL numbering). The GRETIL e-text reads 'sā śuddhiḥ'; the usual reading is 'sā 'śuddhiḥ' (impurity). Linked to the dispute on ritual purity.

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 98: Bhairava in ordinary things
method_summary: Bhairava is present everywhere as being, even in ordinary things; and there is nothing beyond it other than that - this is the non-dual way.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).

name: Vijñāna Bhairava dhāraṇā 99: Equality toward friend and foe
method_summary: Equal toward enemy and friend, equal in honour and dishonour - knowing [this] because Brahman is completely full, one becomes happy.
stage: unmarked in the text; later commentators and translators assign the dhāraṇās to the four upāyas
prerequisites: The text reserves the teaching for those devoted to the teacher's feet, heroic and free of thought-constructs, and forbids giving it to another's disciple, the wicked or the cruel (VBT 157-159).
